title: Treasury and Liquidity
answer: Cash forecasting, currency hedging, idle cash, bank reconciliation and stress testing.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Cash Flow Forecasting
children.blurb: Cash flow forecasting covers the projection of a company's future cash receipts and payments over chosen horizons, from daily to multi-year.

children.name: Currency Hedging
children.blurb: Currency hedging is the practice of managing the impact of exchange rate movements on a company's cash flows, earnings, and balance sheet.

children.name: Idle Cash and Short-Term Yield
children.blurb: Idle cash and short-term yield covers the cash a company holds beyond its immediate operating needs, and the instruments and accounts used to put that cash to work for days, weeks or months.

children.name: Bank Reconciliation
children.blurb: Bank reconciliation is the process of matching transactions recorded in a company's cash ledger against the bank statement for each bank account, then explaining any difference.

children.name: Liquidity Stress Testing
children.blurb: Liquidity stress testing measures whether a firm can keep meeting its payment obligations when funding conditions deteriorate.

sections.body: Treasury and liquidity is the part of finance that watches cash moving in and out, keeps enough money available, and manages risks from currency and interest rates. AI is used in cash forecasting to read bank feeds, ERP data, and payment histories, then produce rolling predictions of daily or weekly balances. In currency hedging, models help estimate exposure and suggest hedge ratios, though execution still runs through human traders and bank platforms. For idle cash, systems scan balances and short term yields to flag surplus that could be invested within policy limits. Bank reconciliation uses matching algorithms and anomaly detection to pair transactions and highlight breaks. Liquidity stress testing uses scenario engines to simulate shocks and estimate how much cash would be needed under different conditions.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is partly solved and partly fragile. Reconciliation is the most mature area, because matching rules and machine learning can handle high volumes of repetitive transactions, but unusual items still need people. Cash forecasting has improved with better data pipelines, yet accuracy falls when payment behavior changes, when subsidiaries report late, or when markets move fast. Currency hedging models can estimate exposure, but they cannot remove uncertainty about rates or counterparty behavior, and governance usually keeps final decisions with treasury teams. Idle cash optimization is constrained by investment policy, credit limits, and accounting rules, so AI mostly ranks options rather than acting alone. Stress testing produces scenarios and ranges, not guarantees, and the quality depends on assumptions that are often incomplete.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section form a chain from seeing cash to protecting it. Cash Flow Forecasting is the starting point, because it builds the baseline view of incoming and outgoing money that the other pages depend on. Currency Hedging follows for readers who need to understand how foreign exchange exposure is measured and managed around that forecast. Idle Cash and Short-Term Yield looks at what to do with balances that are not needed immediately, within policy and risk limits. Bank Reconciliation is the ground level check that keeps the forecast honest by matching what the bank says happened with what the company recorded. Liquidity Stress Testing sits above them all, taking the forecast, the hedges, the cash buffers, and the reconciliation gaps and asking how they hold up under pressure, and across the 432 company pages tracked on this site these five pages are the treasury and liquidity slice of that larger atlas.
